title: Show the cash low point and the upfront-payment lever
decision_task: Whether the owner can fund a play's growth before it pays back.
applies_when: Any play with spend before contribution arrives, especially when scaling spend.
exclusions: Businesses paid upfront with contribution at or above CAC in month 0.
missing_data_behavior: Acquisition cost or contribution unknown: no trough shown; ask for them.
Owner's cash reserve unknown: show the trough and ask whether it's affordable.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing timing: assume contribution starts the month after acquisition, labelled.

decision_branches.if: Trough deeper than the owner's stated reserve
decision_branches.then: Slow spend, ask for upfront or annual payment, or stage the plays.

decision_branches.if: Paid upfront with contribution at or above CAC

implementation_steps: Simulate the monthly cumulative cash for the portfolio over 24 months (DS-FX16).
Report the lowest cash point, its month and the cash breakeven month.
Show the effect of annual prepayment or a deposit.
guardrails: Do not call a play affordable because value exceeds CAC if the trough is larger than the owner's stated cash.
stop_conditions: Pause scaling if the observed trough runs deeper than planned by 25% or more.
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes

interpretation: Interpretation: Skok's trough is about venture-funded scaling. For a small owner, the trough is personal cash.
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed rule: lockedNumbers adds a line 'lowest cash point −X in month M, breakeven month B'.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
hard_failure: Calls it affordable without checking cash

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
